questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{ft}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3{t}^{2}-2t-3$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=6\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=3\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{ft/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-2t-3)\text{d} \\  & ={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-3t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(3)=6.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =(3)^{3}-(3)^{2}-3(3)+C \\ 6 & =27-9-9+C \\ C & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-3t-3.$

questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2-3{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=4\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$) of the particle at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2-3{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =2t-{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2(1)-(1)^{3}+C \\ 4 & =2-1+C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3+2t-{t}^{3}.$

questions.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=6{t}^{2}-12{t}^{5}+4,$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. Find the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}$ given that the particle has velocity $v=3\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$

The speed at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}} $\text{m/s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (6{t}^{2}-12{t}^{5}+4)\text{d}t \\  & =2{t}^{3}-2{t}^{6}+4t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=3.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =2({0}^{3})-2({0}^{6})+4(0)+C \\ 3 & =0+C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2{t}^{3}-2{t}^{6}+4t+3.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =2({2}^{3})-2({2}^{6})+4(2)+3 \\  & =2(8)-2(64)+8+3 \\  & =16-128+8+3 \\  & =-101\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $101\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{ft}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=20t-12{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=8\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (20t-12{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =10{t}^{2}-4{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=8.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =10(1)^{2}-4(1)^{3}+C \\ 8 & =6+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=10{t}^{2}-4{t}^{3}+2.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =10(2)^{2}-4(2)^{3}+2 \\  & =40-32+2 \\  & =10\,\text{ft}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|$, we conclude that the speed of the particle is $10\,\text{ft}/\text{s}.$

questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-5{t}^{4}+2t+2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-8\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-5{t}^{4}+2t+2)\text{d}t \\  & =-{t}^{5}+{t}^{2}+2t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-8.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & =-(0)^{5}+(0)^{2}+2(0)+C \\ -8 & =0+C \\ C & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-{t}^{5}+{t}^{2}+2t-8.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =-(2)^{5}+(2)^{2}+2(2)-8 \\  & =-32+4+4-8 \\  & =-32\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $32\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t),$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{4}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment  $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{1}{4}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)}{4}+C \\ \frac{1}{4} & =-\frac{1}{4}+C \\ C & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)}{4}+\frac{1}{2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s},$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is also  $\frac{3}{4}\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the speed of the particle at the moment $t=\frac{\pi }{3}\,\text{s}$ given that the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$

The speed at the moment $t=\frac{\pi }{3}\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}} $\,\text{m/s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+C \\ \frac{1}{2} & =-2+C \\ C & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{5}{2}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=\frac{\pi }{3}\,\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{5}{2}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-2(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\frac{3}{2}\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=4{sec}^{2}⁡t,$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{ft/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the speed of the particle at the moment $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s}$ given that the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{ft/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$

The speed at the moment $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}} $\,\text{ft/s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 4{sec}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\operatorname{tan}⁡t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =4\operatorname{tan}⁡(0)+C \\ \frac{1}{2} & =0+C \\ C & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{1}{2}+4\operatorname{tan}⁡t.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{1}{2}+4\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+4(1) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}\,\text{ft/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\frac{9}{2}\,\text{ft/s}.$

canonical_examples.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\textrm m / \textrm s^2,$ given by the function $a(t) = 4t^2 - 3t^3,$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\textrm m / \textrm s$ when $t=0 \,\textrm s,$ calculate the velocity (in $\textrm m / \textrm s$) of the particle at time $t.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (4{t}^{2}-3{t}^{3})\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{3}{t}^{3}-\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0) = 2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{4}{3}(0)^{3}-\frac{3}{4}(0)^{4}+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t) = \dfrac{4}{3}t^3 -\dfrac{3}{4}t^4 + 2.$

canonical_examples.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\textrm m / \textrm s^2,$ given by the function $a(t) =2e^{-t}+6t^2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-4 \,\textrm m / \textrm s$ when $t=0 \,\textrm s,$ calculate the speed of the particle at the moment  $t=1\,\textrm{s}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2{e}^{-t}+6{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =2(-{e}^{-t})+\frac{6}{3}{t}^{3}+C \\  & =-2{e}^{-t}+2{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0) = -4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =-2{e}^{-0}+2\cdot {0}^{3}+C \\ -4 & =-2+0+C \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t) = -2  e^{-t}+ 2t^3 -2.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=1\,\textrm{s}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =-2{e}^{-1}+2(1)^{3}-2 \\  & =-2{e}^{-1}+2-2 \\  & =-\frac{2}{e}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\dfrac 2 e\,\textrm{m/s}.$
